newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says nine new oil wells in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says nine new oil wells in 1997.

text.p: The Philippines' Department of Energy said on Monday it expects nine new wildcat oil wells to be drilled in 1997.

According to the department's oil and gas drilling programme, the Philippine National Oil Co-Exploration Corp, the exploration arm of state-owned PNOC, will drill a well in Palawan, southwest Philippines and an off-shore well in the Ragay Gulf in central Philippines.

Shell Exploration B.V., the local exploration arm of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, is planning to drill two wells in its service area in northwest Palawan, both of which are off-shore, the department said.

Atlantic Richfield Co, Trans-Asia Oil & Mineral Development Corp and Occidental Philippines Inc, a unit of Occidental Petroleum, are to drill one off-shore well each while Vulcan Industrial & Mining Corp and Stirling Resources are to drill one on-shore well each.
This year, only three wells were drilled and all proved to be dry wells.
